summary: A scrollbar's end buttons: the step a press moves, the two keys that multiply it by ten and a hundred, and the hold that repeats it faster the longer it is held.

addresses.name: CScrollbar_LessPressed
addresses.comment: **A press of the scrollbar's leftbutton.** Nothing while the bar is switched off (+0xA0's slot 44 answers 3). The step is the declared one in thousandths (+0x48's slot 6, its +8), and a step of exactly 1 is made 10; with the gui's input object (+0x28, +0xA4) answering slot 10 it is multiplied by floor((+0x204 * 10 + 0.0005) * 1000) / 1000, with slot 12 by floor((+0x208 * 100 + 0.0005) * 1000) / 1000 - ten and a hundred, the two fields being 1. In states 4 and 10 (+0x64) it moves the value by -step, +step where +0x23C is set; then state 10 (CScrollbar_MoveBy, noting the player and telling the observers). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scrollbar.md, section 2.

addresses.name: CScrollbar_MorePressed
addresses.comment: **A press of the scrollbar's rightbutton.** Nothing while the bar is switched off (+0xA0's slot 44 answers 3). The step is the declared one in thousandths (+0x48's slot 6, its +8), and a step of exactly 1 is made 10; with the gui's input object (+0x28, +0xA4) answering slot 10 it is multiplied by floor((+0x204 * 10 + 0.0005) * 1000) / 1000, with slot 12 by floor((+0x208 * 100 + 0.0005) * 1000) / 1000 - ten and a hundred, the two fields being 1. In states 5 and 10 (+0x64) it moves the value by +step, -step where +0x23C is set, the step through floor((step / 1000 + 0.0005) * 1000) (CScrollbar_MoveBy, noting the player and telling the observers). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scrollbar.md, section 2.

addresses.name: CScrollbar_LessHeld
addresses.comment: **Each frame the scrollbar's leftbutton is held.** Starts the clock at +0x200 when it reads 0; else sets the time held (+0x228) to the clock's seconds - `held + (seconds - held)`, so the subtractions of the frame before are lost. Then, held over 0.5 (+0x224) * 0.30000001192092896, it takes that off and presses (CScrollbar_LessPressed) while held is still over it: no press for 0.15 s, then one a frame, then more each frame, by the frame rate. A branch for a press at half a second is never reached. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scrollbar.md, section 3.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled; the line 0xA9F9EE..0xA9F9F8 read in the listing (de ea = fsubp st(2), st(2) - st(0)).

addresses.name: CScrollbar_MoreHeld
addresses.comment: **Each frame the scrollbar's rightbutton is held.** Starts the clock at +0x200 when it reads 0; else sets the time held (+0x228) to the clock's seconds - `held + (seconds - held)`, so the subtractions of the frame before are lost. Then, held over 0.5 (+0x224) * 0.30000001192092896, it takes that off and presses (CScrollbar_MorePressed) while held is still over it: no press for 0.15 s, then one a frame, then more each frame, by the frame rate. A branch for a press at half a second is never reached. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scrollbar.md, section 3.

addresses.name: CScrollbar_LessReleased
addresses.comment: Letting go of the leftbutton: state (+0x64) 10, the clock's slot 2 (Reset), the time held 0. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scrollbar.md, section 3.

addresses.name: CScrollbar_MoreReleased
addresses.comment: Letting go of the rightbutton: as CScrollbar_LessReleased, tail-jumping into the clock's Reset. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scrollbar.md, section 3.

addresses.name: CScrollbar_MoveBy
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CScrollbar_MoveBy(void* scrollbar@EAX, int delta@stack:4, bool byPlayer@stack:8, bool notify@stack:12)
addresses.comment: Moves the value (+0x220, a float) by `delta` thousandths: floor((value + 0.0005) * 1000) + delta, kept between +0x38C and +0x390 where +0x394 is set, stored back over 1000. `byPlayer` sets +0x252; `notify` calls slots 2 and 1 of each observer in the list at +0x4C. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scrollbar.md, section 2.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled; `ret 0xC`, the callers load the scrollbar into EAX.

addresses.name: CScrollbar_Construct
addresses.comment: The scrollbar's constructor: writes vftable 0x15FF7A0, makes the two end buttons' CButtonObserver (+0x150, +0x1A8) with the press, hold and let-go handlers, sets +0x204 and +0x208 to 1, +0x224 to 0.5, the range +0x38C/+0x390/+0x394 and +0x23C from its arguments, and takes a clock from g_random_object's slot 1 into +0x200. Read only as far as that. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scrollbar.md, section 1.

addresses.name: CButtonObserver_Init
addresses.no_signature: the observer in EAX and the owner in ECX with eighteen stack dwords
addresses.comment: Fills a CButtonObserver: the observer in EAX, its owner in ECX, and nine handlers each with an adjustment, eighteen stack dwords, into +8..+0x4C; writes vftable 0x15FF6DC. The scrollbar gives its end buttons the first, the second and the third. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scrollbar.md, section 1.

addresses.name: CHighPerfWinClock::Start
addresses.comment: Slot 1: takes the performance counter into +8 and sets the clock running (+0x28 = 0). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scrollbar.md, section 3.

addresses.name: CHighPerfWinClock::Reset
addresses.comment: Slot 2: base (+0x10, +0x14) 0 and stopped (+0x28 = 1), so GetSeconds answers 0. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scrollbar.md, section 3.

structs.name: CScrollbar
structs.comment: A scrollbarType's live object (vftable 0x15FF7A0, the name by the observer convention): its end buttons' step, repeat and range. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scrollbar.md.
structs.evidence: The constructor 0xA9DB30 writes vftable 0x15FF7A0 at 0xA9DBB9 and fills the fields listed.

struct_fields.name: end_state
struct_fields.comment: 10 at rest; 4 or 10 lets the leftbutton's press move it, 5 or 10 the rightbutton's; a held repeat's unreachable branch sets 2. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scrollbar.md, section 2.

struct_fields.name: clock
struct_fields.comment: A clock from g_random_object's slot 1 - a CHighPerfWinClock in the game - started by the first frame of a hold and reset on letting go. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scrollbar.md, section 3.

struct_fields.name: slot10_factor
struct_fields.comment: 1 from the constructor; a press is multiplied by it times ten while the input object's slot 10 is down. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scrollbar.md, section 2.

struct_fields.name: slot12_factor
struct_fields.comment: 1 from the constructor; a press is multiplied by it times a hundred while the input object's slot 12 - likely Ctrl - is down. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scrollbar.md, section 2.

struct_fields.name: value
struct_fields.comment: The value, kept as a float and moved in thousandths. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scrollbar.md, section 2.

struct_fields.name: repeat_base
struct_fields.comment: 0.5 from the constructor; times 0.3 it is the time each repeat of a hold takes off. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scrollbar.md, section 3.

struct_fields.name: held_seconds
struct_fields.comment: The time the end button has been held, set to the clock's seconds each frame. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scrollbar.md, section 3.

struct_fields.name: invert_ends
struct_fields.comment: From a constructor argument; set, the leftbutton adds and the rightbutton takes away. Not the file's `horizontal`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scrollbar.md, section 2.

struct_fields.name: least
struct_fields.comment: The least value in thousandths, kept to where +0x394 is set. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scrollbar.md, section 2.

struct_fields.name: most
struct_fields.comment: The greatest value in thousandths. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scrollbar.md, section 2.

struct_fields.name: is_bounded
struct_fields.comment: Whether a move is kept between +0x38C and +0x390. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scrollbar.md, section 2.

notes: Read against the maintainer's account of the running game, not watched.
